name: Open Internet Access Regulation
evidence_rating: thin to moderate: qualitative Commission/BEREC reviews; one cross-country causal study on investment (negative) and conflicting correlational studies on zero-rating
summary: The EU's net neutrality rules set no measurable targets; Commission reviews in 2019 and 2023 found them applied consistently and still fit for purpose, and EU court rulings in 2020-21 ended most 'zero-rating' offers. Evidence on economic effects is limited and conflicting: one study of 32 OECD countries finds strict net neutrality rules slowed fibre investment, while studies of zero-rating disagree on whether it raised mobile data prices.

indicators.objective: The 2013 'Connected Continent' proposal (COM(2013) 627) had no financial-statement indicators or monitoring section for the open internet provisions; the impact assessment promised an evaluation after four years. Review clause (Art. 9) led to Commission reports in 2019 and 2023

indicators.indicator: No blocking, throttling or discrimination of traffic; end-users' right to access content of their choice
indicators.evidence: Commission (2019, 2023) and BEREC report consistent application and high end-user and content-provider satisfaction; few penalties, all well below maximums. Zero-rating (application-specific zero tariffs) spread to all but two EU countries (186 offers, 2019) until CJEU rulings (2020-21) made them incompatible; BEREC guidelines revised in 2022.

indicators.objective: Single market for electronic communications (whole package)
indicators.indicator: Direct benefit of a telecoms single market about EUR 110bn a year
indicators.evidence: Not evaluated; the figure covered the whole Connected Continent package, most of which was not adopted.

indicators.indicator: Rules should not deter network investment
indicators.evidence: Commission (2019): regulation 'does not seem to affect' ISP investment (stakeholder-based). OECD panel study (Briglauer et al. 2022) finds strict net neutrality rules significantly slow fibre investment and take-up. Evidence conflicts.

indicators.indicator: Commercial practices must not limit end-user rights
indicators.evidence: Mixed: epicenter.works found mobile data prices rose about 2% in markets with zero-rating vs fell about 8% elsewhere (2015-16); Austrian regulator RTR (11,000+ tariffs, 15 countries, 2015-18) found no systematic effect on data caps or price per GB.

literature.citation: European Commission (2013), Impact Assessment on the European Single Market for electronic communications / Connected Continent (executive summary SWD(2013) 332), SWD(2013) 331
literature.title: Impact Assessment on the European Single Market for electronic communications / Connected Continent (executive summary SWD(2013) 332)
literature.headline: Direct benefit of a single market for electronic communications about EUR 110bn a year plus spill-overs; net neutrality part of a wider package (most of which was dropped)
literature.summary_plain: The Commission put the benefit of its wider telecoms package, including open internet rules, at about EUR 110 billion a year, but did not estimate the net neutrality part separately.

literature.citation: European Commission (2019), Report on the implementation of the open internet access provisions of Regulation (EU) 2015/2120, COM(2019) 203
literature.title: Report on the implementation of the open internet access provisions of Regulation (EU) 2015/2120
literature.method: implementation review (NRA and BEREC reports, stakeholder input)
literature.headline: Principles appropriate and effective; implementation consistent; main issues transparency, zero-rating and traffic management; regulation 'does not seem to affect' ISP investment
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's first review found the rules applied consistently and judged that they had not harmed network investment, though without hard data.

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Second report on the implementation of the open internet access provisions of Regulation (EU) 2015/2120, COM(2023) 233
literature.title: Second report on the implementation of the open internet access provisions of Regulation (EU) 2015/2120
literature.method: implementation review (BEREC Opinion BoR(22)163, ICF/WIK study, CJEU case law)
literature.headline: Principles remain relevant; CJEU judgments (2020-21) ruled application-specific zero-tariff options incompatible; legal uncertainty on specialised services/5G slicing may chill investment; few and low penalties
literature.summary_plain: The second review found the rules still fit for purpose, after EU court rulings ended most zero-rating offers, but noted uncertainty about new 5G services.

literature.citation: Briglauer, Cambini, Gugler & Stocker (2022), Net neutrality and high-speed broadband networks: evidence from OECD countries, European Journal of Law and Economics
literature.title: Net neutrality and high-speed broadband networks: evidence from OECD countries
literature.venue: European Journal of Law and Economics
literature.method: panel econometrics with instrumental variables (32 OECD countries, 2003-2019)
literature.headline: Net neutrality regulations have a significant and strong negative impact on fibre investment; strict rules slow fibre deployment; no overall welfare assessment
literature.summary_plain: A study of 32 OECD countries finds strict net neutrality rules slowed investment in fibre broadband, though it does not weigh benefits for content providers or consumers.

literature.citation: epicenter.works (2019), The Net Neutrality Situation in the EU: Evaluation of the First Two Years of Enforcement, NGO report
literature.title: The Net Neutrality Situation in the EU: Evaluation of the First Two Years of Enforcement
literature.method: survey of 186 differential-pricing offers; OLS regression on Commission mobile price data
literature.headline: Zero-rating in all but two EU countries; in markets with zero-rating in both years mobile data prices rose 2% (2015-16) vs fell 8% where none existed; later analysis (excl. Finland) +1% vs -10%
literature.summary_plain: A digital-rights NGO found zero-rating offers spread widely and that mobile data got cheaper more slowly where they existed.
literature.interested_party: Advocacy NGO campaigning for strict net neutrality

literature.citation: Király & Schwarz (RTR) (2019), Zero-Rating in the EU: An empirical investigation into the effects on data caps and prices in 15 countries, Austrian regulator RTR study (presented at Cullen International seminar, 4 Sept 2019)
literature.title: Zero-Rating in the EU: An empirical investigation into the effects on data caps and prices in 15 countries
literature.venue: Austrian regulator RTR study (presented at Cullen International seminar, 4 Sept 2019)
literature.method: panel and quantile regressions with operator fixed effects (11,000+ tariffs, 53 operators, 15 countries, 2015-18)
literature.outcomes: data caps; price per GB; monthly fee
literature.headline: Share of tariffs with zero-rating rose fivefold; effect on included data, price per GB and monthly fee varies strongly across countries, time and app categories, with no identifiable pattern; supports case-by-case assessment
literature.summary_plain: Austria's telecoms regulator found no consistent effect of zero-rating on data allowances or prices across 15 EU countries.
